entities.summary:
Agrippinus of Naples (Agrippinus), a 3rd-century bishop of Naples, played a pivotal role in the early Christian church in the city. 

Born unknown, he succeeded his predecessor to become the sixth bishop of Naples, a position he held until his death in 300 CE. 

Agrippinus was not a martyr, but his legacy as a saint was recognized by the Catholic Church in the 5th century, and his feast day is celebrated on March 17. 

He was instrumental in the development of the Catholic Church in Naples, and his influence can still be felt in the city's Catholic heritage today. 

Agrippinus's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as the Catholic Church continues to venerate him as a saint. 

"May the saints of the Church intercede for us."
